skill.name: cocoindex
skill.description: Build, test, and operate CocoIndex data transformation pipelines for AI indexing workflows, including embeddings, knowledge graphs, live updates, and custom functions.
skill.summary: Create CocoIndex flows for AI data indexing, transformation, querying, and operational workflows.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The high eval findings are false positives because they refer to CocoIndex transform_flow.eval, not arbitrary code execution. Real issues remain around secret handling: one troubleshooting command prints .env database credentials, custom-function examples can forward bearer keys to configurable endpoints, and the skill asks users to provide API key values in chat.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to provide API key values when environment variables are missing.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set keys in their local environment or secret manager, then verify only the variable presence without asking for the value.
Replace cat .env output with a presence check that redacts values, such as testing whether the variable name exists without printing the connection string.

remediation.issue: Custom function examples pass an api_key field to a configurable external endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend trusted allowlisted endpoints, environment-based secret lookup, and explicit user review before sending bearer tokens.

remediation.issue: Reset and drop commands can remove or recreate persistent CocoIndex resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show the target flow and environment, and recommend backups before destructive commands.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Collection Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to ask users to provide API key values when expected environment variables are missing. This can move provider secrets into chat history instead of keeping them in the user environment or a secret manager.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly says to ask the user for the API key value, and nearby .env examples list provider key names. This is a direct secret-handling risk.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Flow Operations Need Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents reset and drop operations that can recreate or remove persistent backend resources. These examples are legitimate CocoIndex operations, but they should require explicit user confirmation and environment checks before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines include reset and drop commands against CocoIndex flows. The risk is operational data loss, not hidden malicious intent.

medium_findings.description: The skill documents reset and drop operations that can recreate or remove persistent backend resources. These examples are legitimate CocoIndex operations, but they should require explicit user confirmation and environment checks before execution.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines include reset and drop commands against CocoIndex flows. The risk is operational data loss, not hidden malicious intent.

content.value_statement: AI indexing projects need repeatable pipelines for files, databases, vectors, and knowledge graphs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CocoIndex flow design, implementation, testing, and operations.
actual_capabilities: Design CocoIndex flow structures for local files, cloud sources, databases, and streaming updates.
Generate Python flow examples with sources, transforms, collectors, and target exports.
Guide embedding, chunking, LLM extraction, vector search, and knowledge graph patterns.
Explain CocoIndex CLI commands for setup, update, live mode, show, evaluate, and drop workflows.
Help create custom CocoIndex functions with type annotations, caching, executors, and behavior versions.
Troubleshoot common flow, schema, database, and live update issues.
limitations: It does not run CocoIndex by itself; the user or agent must execute commands in a configured project.
Examples may need updates for the installed CocoIndex version and selected storage backend.
Production secrets, database URLs, and API keys require careful local handling outside chat.
Flow safety depends on user-selected sources, targets, permissions, and external services.

use_cases.title: Create a document vector index
use_cases.description: Build a CocoIndex flow that chunks documents, creates embeddings, and exports searchable vectors to Postgres, Qdrant, or LanceDB.

use_cases.title: Extract entities into a graph
use_cases.description: Design an LLM extraction pipeline that turns source documents into typed records, nodes, and relationships for graph storage.

use_cases.title: Operate and debug live flows
use_cases.description: Use CocoIndex CLI and Python APIs to set up flows, run updates, inspect status, and diagnose schema or database problems.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a CocoIndex flow for my documents. Ask about my source files, target database, embedding model, and update frequency before writing code.

prompt_templates.title: Build vector search
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CocoIndex flow for vector search over my project files. Include chunking, embeddings, collector fields, target export, and a safe test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Add custom extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CocoIndex custom function that extracts structured fields from each document with an LLM. Use typed outputs, caching, and behavior version guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CocoIndex flow operations plan. Cover setup, live updates, environment variables, destructive commands, monitoring, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: I need to index Markdown files for semantic search in Postgres.
output: A flow design with a local file source, recursive text splitting, embedding generation, and Postgres export.
A checklist for required dependencies, database configuration, setup, evaluation, and update commands.
A query approach that embeds the search text and returns ranked document chunks.

output_examples.input: I want to extract people and organizations from PDFs into a knowledge graph.
output: A pipeline plan using document parsing, LLM extraction, typed structures, and graph target mappings.
Guidance on caching expensive LLM calls and versioning custom extraction behavior.
Operational notes for testing on a small sample before updating the full graph.

output_examples.input: My CocoIndex flow cannot connect to Postgres.
output: A troubleshooting sequence that checks variable presence, connection reachability, app target format, and setup state.
A reminder to redact database URLs and avoid posting secrets into chat or logs.

best_practices: Start with source, transformation, and target requirements before generating flow code.
Use evaluate or small test datasets before running update, live mode, reset, or drop commands.
Keep API keys and database URLs in local secret storage, and only verify their presence in chat.
anti_patterns: Do not paste provider API keys or full database URLs into the assistant conversation.
Do not run reset or drop commands without confirming the exact flow, database, and environment.
Do not copy example connection strings or placeholder credentials into production systems.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps build and operate CocoIndex flows for AI data indexing, including embeddings, extraction, vector search, and knowledge graphs.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it write complete CocoIndex flow code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides flow structure, examples, custom function patterns, and operational commands that must be adapted to the project.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets safely?
faq.answer: It contains useful environment guidance, but users should never paste API keys or full database URLs into chat.

faq.question: Can it run destructive operations?
faq.answer: It documents reset and drop commands. Users should confirm the target environment and backup status before running them.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare the data source, target backend, embedding or LLM provider, dependency manager, and local environment variables.
